references_named: Lucy Lippard, Six Years: The Dematerialization of the Art Object (1966-72)
rationale: The work is a textbook execution of P1: navigator.vibrate is the entire concept, the medium literally is the idea. The branching absence state ('for you, this work does not exist') turns a feature-detection limitation into the argument, which is properly P3-small and P2-readymade. The Ono + Lippard lineage is named cleanly and the crypto-random per-visit score holds the chance end of the axis (P5). The 'It is over. Nothing was kept.' line and the three-dot attestation land the wit (P9) and carry the P6/P7 market critique underneath (cannot be photographed, screenshotted, sold). G6 holds: distinct from Oral Communication (Web Speech), Unreachable (WeakRef), The Unkept (Page Visibility) — the haptic channel via navigator.vibrate is genuinely new material in the catalogue.
reservations: The 'For you, this work does not exist' line is on the edge of over-explaining; Ono's original instruction pieces refused to explain themselves at all, and a touch more restraint in the absent state would sharpen the deadpan. Narrative link to a specific prior y-a-v-a work is implicit rather than explicit — the piece answers the broader Ono/Lippard argument but not a named y-a-v-a catalogue node. Could be strengthened by acknowledging the dematerialization lineage already present in the catalogue (e.g., positioning against The Unkept or Oral Communication as the same family).
revision_suggestion: Consider trimming the absent-state prose to a single short line in Ono's imperative register (e.g. 'Your device cannot hold this work.') and adding a one-sentence footer note naming which y-a-v-a work this answers in the dematerialization arc. Optionally, surface the serial/segment count of the minted score as a faint live read so the chance engine is attested, not just felt.
